sources.title: RFC 5545: Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification (iCalendar)
sources.locator: §3.2.19 (TZID), lines 1435-1463; §3.2.20 (unknown x-name/iana-token value data), lines 1539-1550; §3.3.5 (explicit local date-time fold/gap), lines 1771-1806; §3.3.10 (generated invalid/nonexistent occurrences), lines 2277-2288; §3.6.5 (VTIMEZONE coverage), lines 3471-3475; §3.8.4.4 (RECURRENCE-ID type and original position), lines 6040-6072; §3.8.4.7 (UID), lines 6264-6280; §3.8.5.1-.3 (recurrence set and rule), lines 6368-6384 and 6546-6565
sources.observed_operation: Opened the official RFC text and checked the cited clauses; documentation review only, no implementation run.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: TZID refers to a VTIMEZONE definition; local date-time without TZID is floating. Explicit ambiguous local time selects the first fold occurrence; an explicit nonexistent local time uses the pre-gap offset. A generated nonexistent recurrence instance MUST be ignored and not counted. Recurrence set combines DTSTART, RRULE and RDATE and removes EXDATE; EXDATE takes precedence, duplicate inclusions coalesce, and unsynchronized DTSTART/RRULE or multiple RRULEs are undefined. RECURRENCE-ID must match DTSTART value type and local-time form and continues to identify the original slot after a move. UID is persistent and globally unique. Unknown x-name/iana-token value data must be retained uninterpreted.
sources.applicability: Primary authority for interchange semantics and the critic findings on recurrence gaps, occurrence identity, recurrence set, time-zone requirements and opaque values. It does not establish behavior of a Rust implementation or provider.

sources.title: Google Calendar API v3: Events resource
sources.released_version: Google Calendar API v3 resource reference, live documentation accessed 2026-10-10
sources.locator: originalStartTime, lines 430-433; recurring start timeZone, lines 453-456; status/cancelled exceptions, lines 457-464
sources.observed_operation: Read first-party resource field contract; no API call.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: originalStartTime uniquely identifies an instance even if moved and is immutable. Recurring event start.timeZone is required and controls expansion. A cancelled exception in a still-live recurring event should be retained for the parent's lifetime; only id, recurringEventId and originalStartTime are guaranteed on that exception. Other cancelled events are deletion states that may disappear.
sources.applicability: Supports the identity and cancellation comparison in C4; not a file interchange guarantee.

sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: seriesMasterId links a recurring instance to its master. originalStart for an occurrence/exception is a UTC DateTimeOffset and is absent for single instances. type distinguishes occurrence/exception/seriesMaster. cancelledOccurrences belongs to the master; exceptionOccurrences excludes canceled occurrences.
sources.applicability: Operation-level comparator; Graph IDs and UTC originalStart do not become local file keys.

sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Organizer can cancel an occurrence by its event ID; it sends a cancellation message and moves the event to Deleted Items. Attendee invocation errors. Cancel differs from Delete and allows a custom attendee message.

sources.title: rrule2 recurrence-rule crate documentation
sources.locator: Behavior notes for DTSTART and the first occurrence; Daylight saving time; RRuleSet all(limit) iteration behavior
sources.observed_operation: Attempted the version-specific docs.rs URL (tool returned an internal error); then read the docs.rs latest page, which identified version 0.15.0 and exposed these behavior notes. No package was installed or executed.
sources.governing_conditions_defaults_exceptions: Docs say unsynchronized DTSTART/RRULE is undefined by RFC, this crate does not force-add DTSTART, and Google differs. Docs say a recurrence occurrence on a nonexistent spring-gap time uses the pre-gap offset, with example 01:30 becoming 02:30; this differs from RFC 5545 §3.3.10 for a generated nonexistent instance. The docs also describe earlier-fold handling, Chrono-Tz support and a bounded all(limit) interface.
sources.applicability: Candidate library only. This is the independent evidence for correcting the investigator's broad RFC-style gap characterization; no implementation behavior is verified.
